**Issue #3666 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3666: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 42902302325](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42902302325) on `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-3656-f2be0ce872ba11e8032bdb3120f84bbf37138df7` (`3e93516`, merge_group) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [web (unit 7/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42902302325/job/130154605756) | 9m 41s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42950132252)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`web (unit k/8)` is already at 8 shards, the most a count may be (`MAX_SHARDS` in `.github/ci/matrix.py`, which `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py:74` pins). So the count cannot go up, and the fix has to be how the files are dealt. Vitest's `--shard` deals files by count in path-hash order, not by time. The comment above `web-unit` in `ci.yml` says the same. A few heavy files can therefore land in one shard, as they did in 7/8 (9m 41s).

Done means a sequencer that deals the web's unit tests over the shards by measured time, as e2e's `WEIGHTS` do. It goes in the root `vitest.config.ts`, outside `.github/`, so the CI command stays as it is. Every test must still land in exactly one shard for any count. The slowest of the eight shards should come in clearly nearer to the mean, which the builder shows with before and after timings.

I had no network, no `node_modules` and no CI log, so I do not know which files made 7/8 slow. Step 2 measures that before anything changes. If one single file is the problem, weighting cannot shrink it (see Open questions).

## Files to touch

| File | | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts` | new | `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S`, the `WEIGHTS` table, `dealShards()`. No imports, so Node can load it directly. |
| `apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.ts` | new | Default-exported `WeightedShardSequencer extends BaseSequencer`, overriding `shard()`. |
| `apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts` | new | Tests of `dealShards`, the table and the sequencer. |
| `vitest.config.ts` | change | `test.sequence.sequencer: WeightedShardSequencer`; comment updated. |
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change | Comment only, on the `[web]` table: `unit` stays 8, the files are dealt by weight, the table is `shardWeights.ts`. |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, `crates/`, `spec/` or any other test file. No ruling is involved, so no `spec/rulings/` note. `scripts/ci-scope.sh` needs no change: `apps/web/src/test/*` and `vitest.config.ts` already turn `web` on. Rule 9 is met by the named constant and the named table.

## Steps

1. **Check Vitest's API (5.0.1) before writing code.** Run `grep -rn "class BaseSequencer" -A 14 node_modules/vitest/dist/ --include=*.d.ts`. Confirm all of these:
   - `BaseSequencer` and `TestSpecification` are exported from `vitest/node`.
   - `shard(files)` is the method to override.
   - `this.ctx.config.shard` is `{ index, count }` (1-based) and `this.ctx.config.root` exists.
   - `spec.moduleId` is the file's absolute path.
   - `test.sequence.sequencer` is accepted in the root config.

   Where a name differs, use the real one. If there is no hook that deals shards, write nothing and stop with `"human_required": true`, giving the lines in Open questions.

2. **Measure the current shards, changing no tracked file.** Run `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`. Then run this in the background (`run_in_background`) and wait for it to finish. Do not add or edit any file under `apps/` or the root config until it ends: a new test file would change what the later shards run.

   ```
   for k in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
     pnpm exec vitest run --project web --project edge --project admin --shard=$k/8 \
       --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts' \
       --exclude '**/src/net/promote-production.test.ts' --exclude '**/src/net/promote-staging.test.ts' \
       --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/before-$k.json || true
   done
   ```

   Then print each shard's file count and wall time:

   ```
   python3 -I - before <<'EOF'
   import glob, json, sys
   for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"/tmp/{sys.argv[1]}-*.json")):
       runs = json.load(open(path))["testResults"]
       wall = (max(r["endTime"] for r in runs) - min(r["startTime"] for r in runs)) / 1000
       print(path, len(runs), "files", round(wall), "s")
   EOF
   ```

   Keep this table for the PR description. Whichever shard is slowest locally is the one to compare in step 7.

3. **Write the weights table text.** From the `before-*.json` files, list every file that took 3 s or more, and the five slowest files overall:

   ```
   python3 -I - <<'EOF'
   import glob, json, os
   root = os.getcwd() + "/"
   rows = {}
   for path in glob.glob("/tmp/before-*.json"):
       for r in json.load(open(path))["testResults"]:
           rows[r["name"].replace(root, "")] = round((r["endTime"] - r["startTime"]) / 1000)
   for name in sorted(rows):
       if rows[name] >= 3:
           print(f'  "{name}": {rows[name]},')
   print(sorted(((s, n) for n, s in rows.items()), reverse=True)[:5])
   EOF
   ```

   The first part is the body of `WEIGHTS`. If any file in the last line took over 120 s, follow Open questions (a).

4. **Create `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts`.** Use only erasable TypeScript syntax: no enums, and no imports.
   - A header comment saying what it is: the seconds each web or Worker unit-test file takes, dealt by `dealShards` through `shardSequencer.ts`; `web (unit k/8)` runs the k-th share (#3666). Say why it exists: Vitest's own `--shard` deals by count, so heavy files clustered into one shard, and the count is at its cap of 8. Say how to refresh it: run step 2's loop and list files of 3 s or more. Say that a file not listed counts `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S` and is still run. Copy the tone of `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`'s header.
   - `export const DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S = 1;`
   - `export const WEIGHTS: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = { … }`. Keys are repo-root-relative paths with `/` separators (for example `apps/web/src/cards/art/scene.test.ts`). Values are the whole seconds from step 3.
   - `export function dealShards(paths: readonly string[], count: number, weights: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = WEIGHTS): string[][]`, which deals longest-first, as `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` does:
     - Weight of a path is `weights[path] ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S`.
     - Sort a copy of `paths` by weight descending, then path ascending, so the result never depends on input order.
     - Give each path to the shard with the least load so far (the lowest index on a tie), and add its weight to that load.
     - Return `count` arrays. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on, so write the array reads with `?? 0` or `?? []`.

5. **Create `apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.ts`.**
   - Imports: `relative` and `sep` from `node:path`, `BaseSequencer` and `type TestSpecification` from `vitest/node`, and `dealShards` from `./shardWeights.ts`.
   - `export default class WeightedShardSequencer extends BaseSequencer` with `override async shard(files: TestSpecification[]): Promise<TestSpecification[]>`.
   - Read `{ index, count } = this.ctx.config.shard ?? { index: 1, count: 1 }`.
   - Build `Map<string, TestSpecification>` keyed by `relative(this.ctx.config.root, spec.moduleId).split(sep).join("/")`.
   - Return the specs for `dealShards([...map.keys()], count)[index - 1] ?? []`.
   - Add a header comment: Vitest's `sort()` still orders a shard's files, and a path the table does not know counts `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S`. CI runs from the repo root, so the keys match. Run from another directory, the deal still covers every file once, just by count.

6. **Change the root `vitest.config.ts`.** Add `import WeightedShardSequencer from "./apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.ts";` and put `sequence: { sequencer: WeightedShardSequencer },` inside `test`, after `projects`. Extend the existing comment with a line saying `--shard` is dealt by `shardWeights.ts` (#3666). Do not edit `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` or the CI command.

7. **Write the test file** (see Tests). Then edit the `[web]` comment in `scripts/ci-shards.toml`: keep `unit = 8`, and add that the files are dealt by measured weight (`apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts`), that Vitest's count-based deal had made one shard slow while the count was at its cap (#3666), and that when a shard drifts the fix is to refresh the table, not the count.

8. **Measure again with the new code.** Repeat the step 2 loop with `--outputFile=/tmp/after-$k.json`, then run the step 2 summary with `after`. Check three things:
   - Together the eight `after` shards ran exactly the files the `before` ones ran. Compare `sorted(name)` over both sets of JSON, and also compare the two totals.
   - The slowest `after` wall is no more than 1.25 times the mean of the eight, and lower than the slowest `before` wall.
   - No `after` shard ran fewer than 40 files (a sanity check that the sequencer, not the default, dealt them).

   If any check fails, fix the cause rather than loosening the check. For example, a key that does not match a real path is the likely cause of the 1.25 miss. Put the before and after tables in the PR description.

## Tests

`apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts` starts with `// @vitest-environment node`. Its `describe` title is `"#3666 the web unit tests' weighted shards"`. It uses synthetic paths such as `apps/web/src/f${i}.test.ts` (60 of them) and a synthetic weights map passed as the third argument, so it never depends on the real table.

- `"#3666 every path lands in exactly one shard, for each count from 1 to 8"`: concatenating the shards has the same sorted content as the input, with no duplicates.
- `"#3666 the shards are the same whatever order the paths arrive in"`: the input and its reverse give `toEqual` results.
- `"#3666 no two shards differ by more than the heaviest path"`: with a few heavy synthetic weights (30, 20, 12), max load minus min load is at most 30, for counts 2 to 8.
- `"#3666 a path with no weight counts DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S"`: with `{ "apps/web/src/big.test.ts": 10 * DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S }`, `big.test.ts` plus ten other paths dealt over 2 shards leaves `big.test.ts` alone in its shard.
- `"#3666 WEIGHTS names only files that exist, in whole seconds"`: locate the repo root as `join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../../../..")`, as `net/ci-scope.test.ts` does. For each key, `existsSync(join(root, key))` holds, the weight is a positive integer, and the key ends in `.test.ts` or `.test.tsx`. This stops the table rotting when a file is renamed.
- `"#3666 WeightedShardSequencer.shard runs every file once across a count's shards"`: build a fake context `{ config: { root, shard: { index, count: 3 } } }` and fake specs `{ moduleId: join(root, "apps/web/src/a.test.ts") }`, both cast through `unknown`. For index 1, 2 and 3, `await new WeightedShardSequencer(ctx).shard(specs)`. The three results together are the input, each once.

Commands, in the order to run them:

```
pnpm --dir apps/web test src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
pnpm exec eslint vitest.config.ts apps/web/src/test
```

The `ci-scope` run confirms the web's source scans accept the new files.

## Done when

- [ ] Step 2's before table and step 8's after table are in the PR description. The after check (slowest ≤ 1.25 × mean, below the old slowest) holds, or the PR says plainly which file or which number stops it (Open questions).
- [ ] `unit = 8` is unchanged in `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, and no file under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/` or `.squishy/` is touched.
- [ ] The new test file passes along with `ci-scope.test.ts`, `typecheck`, the root `tsc` and eslint.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: `cargo fmt --check`, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, and the web tests with `--changed origin/main`. The harness's web run needs the new sequencer to load cleanly from the root config.
- [ ] Every decision the task did not settle is recorded with the alternative rejected (see below).

Decisions to record:
- A weighted sequencer rather than raising the count (impossible) or renaming files to move them between shards (breaks on the next added file).
- A `.ts` table rather than JSON, so the config loader and `tsc` need no JSON settings.
- Listing only files of 3 s or more, with a default of 1 s for the rest.
- The files sit under `apps/web/src/test/`, where `ci-scope.sh` already maps them to `web`.

## Risks

- **Vitest 5.0.1's names.** The sequencer API is from memory of earlier versions. Step 1 checks it, and the stop condition is written there.
- **A shard that runs nothing, or a file that runs twice.** The deal is a partition by construction. The first, second and last tests cover it, and step 8 compares the file sets of all eight real shards.
- **Stale weights.** A new file counts 1 s and is still run, so it is never skipped. The rename test fails loudly when a key no longer exists. Drift only costs balance, never coverage.
- **Local timings differ from CI's.** Only the ratios matter for the table. Step 8 compares shard walls on the same machine, so the improvement is real even if CI's seconds are not the builder's.
- **Other runners of Vitest.** Local `pnpm --dir apps/web test` never calls `shard()`, so it is unaffected. Stryker shards its own way (`scripts/mutants.sh`) and never uses `--shard`. The only `--shard` use is `ci.yml:1053`.
- **Flaky timing.** The measurement runs several workers at once, so a file's duration includes contention. Take the 3 s threshold as coarse, not precise.

## Open questions

**(a) Whether weighting is enough.** Weighting cannot split a file that is slow on its own. If a single file measures over 120 s in step 3, or if step 8's slowest shard is still over budget with a balanced deal, the builder must not weaken or skip tests. It records the file name and time in its decisions. Two lines then need a person, since both are under `.github/` or `bot/`:
- `.github/workflows/super.yml`, job `web-extra`: add the file to its `vitest run` path list, so a sweep tail can move to `src/test/daily.ts` (`sweep()`/`daily`) and still run daily.
- `.github/ci/matrix.py`: change `MAX_SHARDS = 8` to `12`. After that, `scripts/ci-shards.toml`'s `unit` can go to 12, and `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` needs the same change at lines 74, 119–135 and its `range(1, matrix.MAX_SHARDS + 1)` loop (it pins `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]` and "from 1 to 8").

**(b) The merge-queue run may have been a one-off slow runner.** The issue gives only the job's total, not its steps, so I could not tell install time from test time. The weighted deal is still worth having: it makes every shard predictable and stops a cluster of heavy files from landing together. If step 2 shows no shard locally above the mean by much, say so in the PR and let the deal go in anyway.
````
